newsitem.title: CHINA: Beijing economy grows by 11.2 pct in first half.
newsitem.headline: Beijing economy grows by 11.2 pct in first half.

text.p: China's capital recorded growth in its gross domestic product of 11.2 percent year-on-year, to 74.41 billion yuan, the Xinhua news agency on Thursday said quoting figures from the Statistics Bureau.

However, this economic foundation was not strong enough to ensure sustained and steady growth, bureau director Tang Long was quoted as saying. He said sluggish demand and an irrational economic structure remained major problems, Industrial production rose by 11.9 percent, the service sector reported growth of 11 percent and agriculture increased by 3.2 percent, Tang said.

He attributed the strong industrial growth to state enterprises, especially technology-intensive firms in the city's Zhongguancun High-Tech Industrial Development Zone, known as China's Silicon Valley, which contributed 60 percent to the growth.
Investment in fixed assets was kept at a low level, with investment in real estate dropping by 7.1 percent, he said without giving an overall figure.

Exports were expected to total $1.1 billion, an increase of 1.4 percent, while imports were $1.46 billion US dollars, up 5.1 percent. The city used overseas investment og $930 million, a rise of 11.2 percent from last year.
The city's fiscal revenue grew 25.1 percent compared with last year to 10.56 billion yuan, 56 percent of the year's target.
Beijing's expenditure in the first half surged 32.5 percent to 8.87 billion yuan, or 38.7 percent of the budgeted figure.

Spending on enterprise renovation jumped 49.5 percent while that on culture and education rose 29 percent. Urban maintenance expenditure rose 43.4 percent while policy-oriented subsidies soared 51.4 percent.
Outstanding deposits in the capital's banking system reached 478.1 billion yuan by the end of June, up 33.6 billion yuan from the beginning of this year.
